public_rationale: OpenAI released GPT-5 on August 7, 2025 [e1]. That day, The Guardian reported Sam Altman's assessment that GPT-5 had not reached AGI, including his concern about its inability to learn continuously [e2]. METR's July 2025 evaluation, published August 7, tested GPT-5 Thinking before release [e3]. It identified seven tasks with successful human baselines where all six model attempts failed, with no identified technical problems or ambiguities [e3]. These validated capability gaps corroborate the explicit assessment of nonattainment and support the forecast under the contract's reading of AGI [e2, e3]. OpenAI also reported strong software-engineering results, but those domain-specific results do not establish broadly general human-level capability [e4].
limitations: The evidence does not supply a universally accepted AGI threshold.
The explicit assessment of nonattainment comes from OpenAI's CEO, as reported by The Guardian [e2].
METR tested GPT-5 Thinking on technical tasks; this was not a comprehensive assessment of every GPT-5 configuration [e3].
METR also found task defects and failures without human baselines; those failures do not carry the same evidential weight [e3].
The assessment concerns the released system, not future derivatives.

statement.excerpt: GPT-5 will not bring us to AGI.
statement.document_title: How China might crush the West in the race to AGI if we don’t up our regulatory game

from_speaker: will not bring us to AGI
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that GPT-5 itself would not achieve broadly general human-level intelligence, including the ability to handle unfamiliar tasks reliably.
I interpret GPT-5 as the released system bearing that name, including its reasoning capabilities. This does not extend the claim to every successor or future system built using GPT-5.
Marcus supplied no numerical test or definition of AGI. Strong performance in individual domains does not alone settle whether intelligence is broadly general.
The forecast has no calendar deadline. Release and substantive capability evaluations can nevertheless settle this model-specific prediction.
criteria.support_condition: GPT-5 is released, and substantive evaluations identify material gaps in general human-level capability, corroborated by an explicit assessment that the released system has not achieved AGI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The released GPT-5 demonstrates broadly general human-level intelligence through credible, independently corroborated evaluations across unfamiliar tasks and domains.

evidence.locator: Footnote discussing investigation of 28 tasks with no successful runs
evidence.explanation: METR tested GPT-5 Thinking before release and identified seven tasks with human success baselines and genuine repeated failures. This corroborates material capability gaps, although the study was not a comprehensive AGI test.

evidence.excerpt: gpt-5-thinking and gpt-5-thinking-mini are our highest-scoring models on this benchmark.
evidence.explanation: The system card documents substantial software-engineering capability and improvement over earlier OpenAI models. This weighs against portraying GPT-5 as generally incapable, but does not establish AGI.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The launch-day assessment explicitly states that GPT-5 had not reached AGI [e2]. Release documentation [e1] and METR's substantive evaluation, available that day [e3], jointly meet the early-resolution rule: the named system was released, and validated capability gaps corroborated nonattainment.
